full_judgment:
Mr. K. M. Masan, J. : Petitioner seeks leave to appeal from the judgment and order dated 9.6.1999 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2006 of 1997 rejecting the application summarily. 

 2. The complainant-petitioner filed a petition of complaint before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence alleged against the accused persons in C. R. Case No. 2233 of 1995. The learned Metropolitan Magistrate by his order dated 24.4.1996 discharged the accused per-sons under Section 241A of the Criminal Procedure Code on the ground that the charge appeared to be groundless. Thereafter the complainant-petitioner moved the learned Sessions Judge in revision being Criminal Revision No. 173 of 1996 and the learned Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Dhaka by the judgment and order dated 27.7.1997 rejected the criminal revision and affirmed the judgment and order of discharge passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate. Against the judgment a Rule was obtained by the complainant-petitioner from the High Court Division in a revisional application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 19.5.1998 being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2006 of 1997. On 27.11.1997 when the rule was taken up for hearing by the High Court Division none appeared and the same was discharged with observation that the court found no substance in the rule. 

 4. The learned. Advocate for the petitioner argues that the High Court Division ought to have given him an opportunity to appear in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2006 of 1997 and dispose of the rule on merit and not by doing so occasioned failure of justice causing serious prejudice to the petitioner. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2006 of 1997 that though the rule was discharged in the absence of the petitioner's lawyer but the facts and circumstances involved were duly considered. The proper forum against such judgment and order would have been an appeal before the Appellate Division and not an application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In view of the above the leave petition is dismissed.
